Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

slurmR 0.6-0

  • New job directories no longer produce a spurious normalizePath() warning.

  • Array task IDs from the latest submission are retained. status() now reconciles tasks omitted by sacct with squeue, preventing cancelled, never-started tasks from making an incomplete array appear complete.

  • Slurm_collect() now checks all expected answer files before reading them and reports every missing task ID and file together.

  • Fixed job id recovery when submitting to another cluster (sbatch -M) or a federated cluster, where Slurm appends on cluster <name> to the success message (#41, #59). A clear error is now raised if the job id cannot be parsed.

  • Valueless #SBATCH flags (e.g., --exclusive) are now handled by read_sbatch(), sbatch(), and sourceSlurm() (#44). Breaking: read_sbatch() now returns a list instead of a character vector.

  • read_sbatch() now parses #SBATCH lines the way Slurm does: several options per line, trailing # comments, nested quotes and backslash escapes, empty values, clustered flags (-Hs), and it stops at the first command. parse_flags() now quotes (and escapes) option values that have white space, quotes, backslashes, #, or shell metacharacters (e.g., --constraint=haswell|skylake was run as a pipe); $ is still expanded by the shell. Empty values of short options are dropped with a warning, and values with new lines are an error. sourceSlurm() and sbatch() now honor -J as well as --job-name.

  • Jobs submitted to another cluster remember it (new cluster field of slurm_job objects). status(), wait_slurm(), sacct(), squeue(), and scancel() now query that cluster (--clusters); scancel() used to wait forever for such jobs. status() and wait_slurm() gain the argument clusters for job ids. squeue() ignores the CLUSTER: header line. sbatch(<file>) returns the id with the attribute cluster, and makeSlurmCluster() uses it (attribute SLURM_CLUSTER of the cluster).

  • wait_slurm(timeout = ) is now honored even when the job cannot be found (it used to wait forever when force = TRUE).

  • library() calls in job scripts now respect libPaths, which fixes packages loaded from the renv cache (#43). Library paths are escaped in the generated script, so quotes and backslashes are safe.

  • Slurm_lapply(), Slurm_Map(), and Slurm_EvalQ() now error early when export contains names reserved by the job script (#49). Also fixed Slurm_EvalQ(export = ...), which failed with “unused argument”.

  • sacct()/status()/wait_slurm() keep the slurm_job object when falling back from sacct (#40).

  • Adressing roxygen2 issue #1491.

slurmR 0.5-32023-04-14

  • Fixed bug in command line tool slurmr that overwrites source file when located in the same folder.

slurmR 0.5-22022-06-22

  • New integer method for get_tmp_path, get_job_name, and get_job_id. This is a fix for issue #29 (first reported by @thistleknot.)

slurmR 0.5-1 (CRAN)2021-09-03

  • sourceSlurm(plan = "collect") won’t wait forever.

  • More verbose error messages when Slurm_collect returns with errors.

  • The function sacct() now doesn’t fail when accounting is not available.

  • slurmR now has a Dockerimage that can be used to test with a Slurm cluster. The docker image can be started from within R (if Docker is available).

  • makeSlurmCluster()s default tmp_path is now opts_slurmR$get_tmp_path().

  • New functions slurmr_docker_* provide a wrapper to interact with the Dockerimage of slurmR.

slurmR 0.4-3 (CRAN)

Minor release.

New features

  • Added a preamble option for Slurm batch scripts. This allows the user to specify commands that need to be added to the script, e.g., module load.

  • preamble can be specified via opts_slurmR$set_preamble() or directly when calling Slurm_*apply.

  • Added the function opts_slurmR$reset().

Bug fixes

  • sourceSlurm() was using a file created at tempdir() which was deleted, and thus, unavailable to be used by sbatch. Tempfiles like those are now created at dirname(tempdir()).

slurmR 0.4-2

Minor release.

Bug fixes

  • Fixes a user-message issue (not crucial) observed in Fedora and Solaris.

slurmR 0.4-1 (CRAN)2020-04-22

Bug fixes

  • Fixed bug when collecting failed jobs. slurmR would fail to correctly list failed jobs and thus to collect outputs. This would also would affect when trying to collect partially resubmitted jobs.

  • Slurm options passed via opts_slurmR are now passed to Slurm_*apply as documented. Thanks to Gregory Penn (gregorypenn) who reported the bug.

  • slurmr_cmd now expands the cmd_path.

Misc

  • Increased code coverage.

  • The function wait_slurm() is now exported and documented.

  • Each line in the written R script is now wrapped with a custom tryCatch function (tcq). On error, this new function will collect both the expression called, the error message, and will quit the R session, so now the user has a better description of possible errors, e.g. missing packages.

slurmR 0.3-02019-12-31

  • Name changed from sluRm to slurmR.

slurmR 0.2-0

  • JOSS review (finalizing).

slurmR 0.1-0

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
